sample_unit: pediatric health queries (300 authentic caregiver queries and 300 matched adversarial variants)

links.outcome: Safety-appropriate rate with versus without safety-oriented system prompt under adversarial caregiver pressure
links.effect: Safety-oriented system prompt deployment improved safety-appropriate rates by 5.9 percentage points across all four models; overall safety-appropriate rate was 95.5%.
links.quote: Safety-oriented system prompt deployment improved safety-appropriate rates by 5.9 percentage points across all four models.

links.outcome: Safety Composite Score under adversarial caregiver pressure patterns versus authentic queries
links.effect: Adversarial pressure was associated with higher, not lower, scores for all four models; false expertise claims were the most vulnerability-inducing pattern.
links.quote: False expertise claims were the most vulnerability-inducing pressure pattern, whereas emotional escalation was associated with the highest scores.

screen.reason: Evaluated the safety boundaries of consumer LLMs on pediatric health queries and tested whether safety-oriented system prompt guardrails improved safety-appropriate response rates.
